rigorItems.text: Treatment is adapted to each patient, not chosen by default
Donor sperm treatments are available for women without a partner and women with a female partner
IVF can also be used for single motherhood and shared motherhood in female couples
Clinical decisions are explained carefully and without assumptions
Medical expertise is combined with emotional sensitivity and inclusive care

blocks.title: For single women considering donor insemination
intro: For many single women, donor insemination may be the most natural first step when fertility conditions are favorable.
blocks.boxIntro: This option may be particularly suitable when:
items: Age is still on your side
Ovarian reserve is normal or acceptable
At least one fallopian tube is patent
A less invasive treatment is medically appropriate
closing: What matters is assessing whether this route is likely to offer a good chance of pregnancy in your case, or whether another strategy would be more effective from the start.
blocks.hint: Thinking about becoming a mother on your own? Understand when donor insemination, IVF or another route may be right for you.

blocks.title: For female couples considering donor sperm treatment
intro: For female couples, fertility treatment is not a one-size-fits-all decision.
Some couples may choose donor insemination as a first option. Others may prefer IVF, whether for medical reasons or because they want to explore a shared motherhood pathway.
closing: This allows treatment to be planned with both medical safety and respect for the family project.
blocks.hint: Explore your options with donor sperm and understand whether insemination, IVF or shared motherhood may fit your family project.

blocks.title: For female couples interested in shared motherhood (ROPA)
intro: IVF allows two women to share motherhood through the ROPA method, where one partner provides the eggs and the other carries the pregnancy.
For couples considering ROPA, the decision usually involves more than fertility alone.
blocks.boxIntro: It may also include questions such as:
items: Which partner is better suited to provide the eggs
Which partner will carry the pregnancy
Whether ovarian reserve, age, or timing influence the decision
What treatment plan is medically and emotionally most appropriate for both of you
blocks.hint: Considering shared motherhood? Learn how ROPA works and what medical factors may influence the best plan for both of you.

blocks.title: For women who want to understand whether IVF is the better first step
intro: Not every patient is best served by starting with insemination.
blocks.boxIntro: IVF may be more appropriate when:
items: There have already been unsuccessful inseminations
A couple is considering ROPA from the outset
closing: That is why the right first step is not always the simplest one, but the one that best fits the medical reality.
blocks.hint: Not sure whether to start with insemination or go directly to IVF? Download the guide to understand what may make sense in your case.

processSteps.title: Expert fertility assessment
processSteps.text: We review your age, ovarian reserve, reproductive goals, and any prior fertility history to understand which treatment approach is most appropriate.

processSteps.title: Individualized treatment recommendation
processSteps.text: We explain whether donor insemination, IVF, or ROPA is likely to be the best fit based on your medical profile and family project.

processSteps.title: Treatment planning and donor coordination
processSteps.text: If donor sperm is needed, the process is coordinated according to clinical criteria and Spanish legal standards regarding confidentiality and donor matching.

processSteps.title: Treatment and follow-up
processSteps.text: Whether the recommended path is insemination or IVF, you continue with a structured medical process and follow-up tailored to your case.

intlFaqs.q: Can I start the process before traveling?
intlFaqs.a: Yes. The first step can begin with expert consultation and fertility assessment planning, so you can understand your options before organizing treatment travel.

intlFaqs.q: Will I know which treatment is best before coming to Barcelona?
intlFaqs.a: In many cases, yes. Initial evaluation and medical review can help clarify whether insemination, IVF, or shared motherhood should be explored first.

intlFaqs.q: Who will support me during treatment?
list: Professionals experienced in donor sperm treatment and IVF
Staff used to caring for patients who may need remote planning before treatment

realFaqs.q: Can single women have fertility treatment at FIVClinic?
realFaqs.a: Yes. FIVClinic treats women seeking motherhood without a male partner.

realFaqs.q: How is the sperm donor selected?
realFaqs.a: Donor matching is based on physical characteristics and blood group, seeking the greatest physical and immunological similarity possible, within the Spanish legal framework for anonymous donation.

realFaqs.q: Do you offer treatment for female couples?
realFaqs.a: Yes. Donor insemination can be used for women with a female partner, and IVF can also be used for shared motherhood through the ROPA method.

realFaqs.q: Will I know the identity of the donor?
realFaqs.a: No. Sperm donation in Spain is anonymous and confidential under the applicable legal framework.

realFaqs.q: Is donor insemination an option for both single women and female couples?
realFaqs.a: Yes. It can be an appropriate option for women without a partner and for women with a female partner.

realFaqs.q: How do I know whether I should start with insemination or IVF?
realFaqs.a: That depends on factors such as age, ovarian reserve, tubal status, and the treatment goals of the patient or couple. The right approach should always be individualized.
ROPA is an IVF treatment in which one woman provides the eggs and the other carries the pregnancy, allowing two women to share motherhood.

realFaqs.q: Can I start the process if I live outside Barcelona or outside Spain?
realFaqs.a: Yes. The process can begin with consultation and planning before travel, if needed.
